variables.title: Variables
variables.notes: Variables begin with an uppercase letter.

data_types.title: Data Types
data_types.notes: Adapted: Datalog defines relations (tables) and typed attributes.

operators.title: Operators
operators.notes: Logical and arithmetic conditions in rule bodies.

conditionals.title: Conditionals
conditionals.code:
grade(X, "A") :- score(X, S), S >= 90.
grade(X, "B") :- score(X, S), S >= 80, S < 90.
conditionals.notes: Adapted: Conditionals are modeled by multiple rules with different conditions.

for_loop.title: For Loop
for_loop.code:
path(X, Y) :- edge(X, Y).
path(X, Y) :- edge(X, Z), path(Z, Y).
for_loop.notes: Adapted: Iteration is expressed via recursive rule evaluation.

while_loop.title: While Loop
while_loop.code:
ancestor(X, Y) :- parent(X, Y).
ancestor(X, Y) :- parent(X, Z), ancestor(Z, Y).
while_loop.notes: Adapted: Datalog's fixed-point semantics act as a while loop until no new facts are found.

functions.title: Functions
functions.code: grandparent(X, Y) :- parent(X, Z), parent(Z, Y).
functions.notes: Adapted: Logic rules replace functions, generating relations.

arrays.title: Arrays
arrays.notes: Adapted: Relations act as unordered sets/arrays.

maps.title: Maps
maps.notes: Adapted: Key-value stores are modeled as binary relations.

error_handling.title: Error Handling
error_handling.notes: Adapted: Datalog has no runtime errors; you write rules to find inconsistent data.

comments.title: Comments
comments.code:
-- Single-line comment in Datalog
/* Multi-line comment */
comments.notes: Datalog uses -- for line comments and /* */ for blocks.

numbers.title: Numbers & Decimal Data
numbers.notes: Datalog represents exact decimal precisions alongside standard integer types.

booleans.title: Booleans & Predicates
booleans.code:
-- Three-valued logic (TRUE, FALSE, UNKNOWN)
WHERE status = 'ACTIVE' AND deleted_at IS NULL
booleans.notes: Datalog evaluates predicates using declarative boolean conditions with NULL semantics.

type_casting.title: Type Casting (CAST/CONVERT)
type_casting.notes: Datalog casts types using CAST(expr AS target_type) expressions.

strings.title: Strings & Text Literals
strings.code: SELECT 'String literal' AS col, N'Unicode text' AS unicode_col;
strings.notes: Datalog encloses character literals in single quotes with optional N prefix for Unicode.

string_formatting.title: String Concatenation
string_formatting.code: SELECT CONCAT('User: ', username, ' (', email, ')') FROM users;
string_formatting.notes: Datalog formats and joins textual columns using CONCAT or string concatenation operators.

pattern_matching.title: Pattern Matching (LIKE & CASE)
pattern_matching.code:
SELECT CASE 
    WHEN score >= 90 THEN 'A'
    WHEN score >= 80 THEN 'B'
    ELSE 'C'
END AS grade
WHERE email LIKE '%@example.com';
pattern_matching.notes: Datalog performs conditional classification via CASE WHEN and pattern search with LIKE.

range.title: Ranges (BETWEEN & LIMIT/OFFSET)
range.notes: Datalog defines range intervals with BETWEEN and pagination ranges via LIMIT/OFFSET.

iterators.title: Cursors & Window Functions
iterators.notes: Datalog processes ordered sequences set-by-set using window functions or procedural cursors.

oop_classes.title: Schemas & Tables (Entities)
oop_classes.notes: Datalog structures entities through relational tables, constraints, and views.

lists.title: Tables & Arrays
lists.code:
-- Array or temporary result table
SELECT ARRAY[1, 2, 3] AS num_list;
lists.notes: Datalog supports array column types or relation rowsets representing lists.

tuples.title: Rows & Composite Types
tuples.notes: Datalog represents tuples as table rows or composite record types.

sets.title: Set Queries (UNION, INTERSECT)
sets.notes: Datalog combines dataset results using relational algebra (UNION, INTERSECT, EXCEPT).

modules_import.title: Schemas & Extensions
modules_import.code:
CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS "uuid-ossp";
SET search_path TO my_schema, public;
modules_import.notes: Datalog manages namespaces and modular capabilities through schemas and extensions.
